Samir — thanks, and great to meet the Helios team.

We can take ownership of the benchmarking blocks for the MAP. I sketched a short plan below (high level) and attached a lightweight runbook (redwood_runbook_v0.1.pdf) with phases and responsibilities. Marissa will lead execution; Jonas will validate acceptance gates.

Proposed MAP benchmarking scope (summary)
- Goal: Produce a reproducible results package that validates Redwood Dedicated meets Helios traffic SLOs and defines fallback behavior for hosted variant.
- Phases:
  1) Smoke (sanity): single-instance correctness, basic latency/TTFT sanity checks, <2 hours.
  2) Steady-state: 4–8 hour run with customer-provided trace replay, measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and resource utilization.
  3) Stress: progressive concurrency ramp to target concurrency + 25% to surface contention and degradation modes.
- Workload slicing (we will request CSV with sample traces): small chat-like requests (avg 64 tokens), medium completions (avg 256 tokens), batch embeddings (if relevant).
- Acceptance (initial suggestion):
  - TTFT (95th) <= 400ms for small requests under steady-state
  - P95 latency for full response <= 1.2s for medium requests
  - Sustained throughput >= 120 req/s for medium payloads at concurrency 32
  - No more than 1% error rate and no unhandled OOMs during stress run

Open items for you:
- Can you confirm the three representative payload slices and share a sanitized samples CSV?
- Any specific percentile targets Helios must certify for procurement?

Timeline
- We can start smoke + steady-state next week if we receive the CSV by EOD Mon (6/28). Full stress run + deliverable (results summary + artifacts) in 72 hours after steady-state — estimate completion by 7/9 if CSV arrives on 6/28.

I attached a short runbook for clarity. If that timeline doesn't work, we can compress runs but will call out caveats in the deliverable.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Director | Redwood Inference

Samir / Vanessa — jumping in with a more concrete set of SLOs and measurement definitions we will use in the MAP. These are intentionally conservative for Dedicated; we'll note fallback/hosted expectations in the report.

Measurement rules (what we'll measure)
- TTFT: measured from request reception to first token emitted (client RTT excluded)
- Full response latency: measured until final token emitted
- Throughput: successful requests/sec (steady-state windowed average) and tokens/sec for token-bound workloads
- Concurrency: number of simultaneous active requests at the model server layer
- Resource signals: GPU utilization, memory headroom, queue length, and kernel stall counters (where available)

Suggested SLOs (Dedicated baseline)
- TTFT (95th) <= 350ms for small payloads (avg 64 tokens)
- Full response latency (95th) <= 1.0s for 128-token responses; (95th) <= 1.6s for 256-token responses
- Steady throughput: >= 150 req/s for medium payloads (128 tokens) sustained over a 10-minute window at concurrency 24
- Concurrency resilience: when concurrency ramped to 1.25x target, p95 latency may degrade but error rate must remain <2%

Acceptance criteria (what will mark the MAP pass)
- Results summary with reproducible commands + workload CSV
- Baseline and stress run logs, and a small artifacts bundle (prometheus export + kernel traces where applicable)
- A short gov doc in the MAP that describes recommended guardrails (batching, cache TTLs, and quantization guidance)

Execution notes:
- We'll run replay on a staging Dedicated pool matched to your planned capacity. If Helios wants a different hardware profile, note it in the CSV.
- For fairness, we will run each steady-state slice 3x and report the median behavior.

If that looks good, please share the CSV and any hard constraints (e.g., must certify p99 < X). Also indicate if you want embeddings included in the same pass.

Marissa Cole
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
